done.why: On my fourth death a guard in the past vaporized me, and the old man's voice ended it: 'Good night, oh worthy adventurer.' After that I was hanging in a Void where nothing more could happen, so the game was over and I left.

about: You've come down an endless stair into the ruins of the Great Underground Empire. An old man at the end is testing whether you're worthy, and he keeps giving your life back each time you die. The trials are about holding back and about giving things up. You fight a hooded double and find your own face under the hood. You let a thief take a chest and end up with only a plain staff. A freezing lake takes everything you carry. A golden time machine sends you back to the year before the Crown Jewels were dedicated. It's a quiet, sad place full of failed engineering and rusting exhibits.

ending.what: A losing ending. I went back to 776 in the Temporizer, opened the museum door while the guards were still outside, and a guard vaporized me. The voice in the void said it had perhaps been seeking someone else and wished me good night, and the game left me in a permanent Void.

moments.note: The rock description ('The rock has the look of a thing that has been invited many times') made me want to examine everything.
Climbing down the rope, then something moving at the top of the cliff and the rope twitching. Good, ominous foreshadowing.
Tying the rope to the chest got it hauled straight up by a laughing man who left me stranded.
Three waits in a row gave me the same lock-trying message word for word. I couldn't tell if anything was progressing.
He came back, pulled me up and gave me the staff. The waiting paid off, and the varied sounds from above (coins being counted, pacing) were lovely.
'swim' got 'Go jump in a lake!' and that's exactly the command that worked.
Jumping in made me drop the bread and staff too, even though the shore warning only mentioned the light and the sword.
The Scenic Vista table teleported me to Room 8 and I got to keep the grue repellent. Clever device.
With the repellent on, I made it through the grue-filled dark to the Key Room.
Dropped down the manhole into the aqueduct and couldn't climb back. The only other way out was a broken arch. Trapped.
'throw key at balcony' just said 'Thrown.' The key had landed on the arch at my feet.
Jumping from the arch killed me, but the old man brought me back and scattered my things around the early areas.
Pulling the hood off the beaten figure and seeing my own face turn into the old man's. Strong scene.
The repellent was single-use and ran out ('The repellent is all gone') with no warning. Then the grue lair ate me.
'hello sailor' worked on the Viking ship and he threw me a vial.
I turned the lamp off because the text said a *lit* thing dies in the lake. It went under and was ruined for good anyway. That felt like the warning misled me.
Used the vista teleport to leave the burning torch in Damp Passage, the only way I could think of to get light back north.
Ran through one dark room and found the torch still burning. A plan of my own worked.
The earthquake had opened a cleft by the Great Door into the Royal Museum.
The jewel plaque gave the date 777 GUE and the golden machine had a three-digit dial. Satisfying to connect them.
In the past the jewel room door was locked by the departing guards and the stairs south ended blindly. No way to reach the ring.
Opened the door twice while the guards were there and got vaporized. Final death. I never found out what the invisibility potion was for.

wished: I wished the lake warning had said that any lamp is ruined, lit or not. I turned mine off on purpose and lost it anyway.
I wished I'd had some hint that the grue repellent was single-use before I used it.
I wished I could catch the shiny object in the lake sand. It slipped away every time I tried.
I wished I could get into the jewel room in 776 or find out what the vial did. Drinking it had no visible effect.
I wished I could try the Royal Puzzle, which was right there under the hole.
I wished I could pull the Elvish sword out of the rock myself and not just have it appear in a fight.
I wished 'ask man about staff' had given the thief some dialogue. It just said 'Nothing happens.'

lines.line: The rock has the look of a thing that has been invited many times.
lines.why: Dry humour that also told me not to bother tugging the sword. It set the tone.

lines.line: something that is not a tree moves against the light, and the rope twitches once, as though somebody up there had a hand on it and had just taken it off.
Above you, coins: counted, by the sound, one at a time, by somebody who does not trust his own arithmetic and starts again.
lines.why: Turned waiting into a little scene in sound.

lines.line: with deep and sorrowful eyes, which sit oddly in a face like his, as though they had been borrowed from somebody graver.
lines.why: Hinted the thief was really the old man in disguise.

lines.line: You cannot read the language, but the pictures read you: the flames are leaping up at a window, the statues stand either side of a way, and the old man is waiting.
lines.why: A lovely turn of phrase and a map of what's ahead.

lines.line: You stood there, not long ago. It is strange to be the view.
lines.why: Looking down from the aqueduct at the balcony I'd stood on earlier. My favourite line.

lines.line: recoil in horror at the sight of your own face, weary and wounded.
lines.why: The emotional centre of the game for me.

lines.line: Your lamp goes under with the rest. There is a hiss, a brief glow in the water below you, and then not.
lines.why: Beautiful, but it cost me my old friend the lantern even though I'd turned it off.

lines.line: pulls a waffle out of his garment, and vaporizes you with a flick of his finger.
lines.why: An absurd death after a lot of solemn writing. It made me laugh even as it ended the game.

fun.why: The high points were very good: the thief paying off (27), the vista teleport (85), the hood unmasking (144) and my torch plan (233). But three deaths, losing the lamp to a misleading warning (203) and getting stuck in the aqueduct (120) wore me down. The game ended badly at 314.

engagement.why: I kept wanting to see the next place. The earthquake opening the museum (242) and the 777 plaque clue (251) pulled me back in after the setbacks.

difficulty.why: The puzzles themselves were fair: the sailor, the hood, the time dial. What made it hard was resources running out with no warning. The repellent was gone after one use (166) and the lamp was ruined even though I'd turned it off (203). Being trapped in the aqueduct (120) and getting killed in the past (314) both felt punishing, not clever.

interestingness.why: Being tested by a mysterious old man who keeps reviving you is a strong frame. The double under the hood (144), the thief with borrowed eyes (29) and the time travel (262) all fit together around restraint and worthiness.

prose.why: Nearly every examine gave me something precise and melancholy, often funny too: the rock (7), the coin-counting (21), the aqueduct (66), 'It is strange to be the view' (117) and the hissing lamp (203).
